Set to a driver with diff.<driver>.textconv, git runs that command on each version and diffs the text it prints. The conversion is one-way and is for reading: only git diff and the git log family use it, and git format-patch never does. diff.<driver>.cachetextconv = true caches the output in refs/notes/textconv/<driver>. Performing text diffs of binary files
Unset (-merge), a merge keeps the current branch's version and reports a conflict. This suits files whose lines can't be merged meaningfully.
A built-in macro attribute that equals -diff -merge -text. Custom macros are defined with [attr]<name> lines, only in top-level attribute files.
The filter attribute names a filter driver that converts a file between its form in the working tree and the form git stores.
The driver's git/attributes/filter/clean command runs on check-in. git add feeds it the working file on standard input and stores its standard output as the blob.
The driver's git/attributes/filter/smudge command runs on checkout. Git feeds it the blob and writes its output to the working tree.
Either command can be left out.
git/attributes assigns a driver to paths, such as *.als filter=als. The commands are defined in git configuration, which each clone sets for itself:

A clone whose configuration doesn't define the driver passes content through unchanged, and so does a command that exits with a non-zero status. filter.<driver>.required = true makes both an error, for content that is unusable without the filter, such as encrypted files.
%f in a command is replaced with the path being filtered. The file on disk may not exist or may hold other content, so a filter reads only standard input.
filter.<driver>.process runs one long-lived command for a whole git command instead of one per file, and takes precedence over clean and smudge. git/lfs uses it. Long Running Filter Process
Running clean on its own output changes nothing. Smudge followed by clean gives the same result as clean alone.
After changing the clean command, git add --renormalize . stores existing files again through the new command.

merge.renormalize = true runs a virtual checkout and check-in on all three versions in a merge, so a file stored before the filter existed merges cleanly with one stored after. Merging branches with differing checkin/checkout attributes
Git compares a working file with the index by running clean on it. A working file that differs from smudge's output, but cleans to the stored blob, counts as unchanged.
gzip -dc decompresses on clean. With -f, gzip passes input that isn't gzip through unchanged, so clean accepts its own output.

A gzip header records the original file name and modification time, so compressing the same data twice gives two different files. gzip -n leaves both out, and smudge then writes the same file in every clone. RFC 1952: Member format
A filter changes what the repository stores, and git diff then compares the stored form directly.
diff.<driver>.textconv leaves the repository storing the original file and changes only what git diff and git log -p show, as git/attributes describes.
Ableton/Live/Idea/Store-Ableton-in-the-Garden weighs a filter that stores Ableton Live Sets as XML.
The command of a git/attributes/filter driver that converts a working-tree file into the form git stores. It is defined as filter.<driver>.clean in git configuration.
git add feeds it the working file on standard input and stores its standard output as the blob.
git status and git diff also run it to compare a working file with the index, so a working file that cleans to the stored blob counts as unchanged.
Running clean on its own output should change nothing.
git/lfs cleans a large file into a small pointer file and keeps the content outside the repository.
Not the same as git clean, which deletes untracked files: git/clean.
The command of a git/attributes/filter driver that converts a stored blob into the file written to the working tree. It is defined as filter.<driver>.smudge in git configuration.
On checkout, git feeds it the blob on standard input and writes its standard output to the working tree. Clone, switch and git reset --hard write files the same way.
Smudge followed by git/attributes/filter/clean should give the same result as clean alone.
git/lfs smudges a pointer file back into the large file it names, downloading the content when the clone doesn't have it.
normally, git clean will not recurse into subdirectories, but git clean --directory will.

A secure, cross-platform Git credential helper (git-credential-manager, "GCM") that stores and retrieves HTTPS credentials in the OS keychain and handles browser-based OAuth sign-in for GitHub, Azure DevOps, Bitbucket and GitLab.

Installed on macOS by the Homebrew cask git-credential-manager, which unpacks into /usr/local/share/gcm-core. Upgrading the cask runs sudo /usr/local/share/gcm-core/uninstall.sh, so it is declared in Brewfile.privileged and upgraded by mise run brew:privileged.
